# Vairë

> Vairë the Weaver weaves all that has ever been in the halls of Mandos.

*Valar — Valier; the Weaver*

## Overview

Vairë records the past in a vast tapestry, giving the deeds of Eä enduring form.

## Identity

- **Title:** The Weaver
- **Role:** Weaving, history and the tapestry of time
- **Spouse / consort:** Mandos (Námo)
- **Familiar symbols:** woven story; web of time
- **Kindred:** Valier

## Names and Etymology

The name **Vairë** is used throughout Tolkien's published legends for this figure.
Where an alternative name is known, it is preserved here as a secondary epithet rather than treated as a separate character.

## Character and Domain

In the Ainulindalë and Valaquenta, Vairë is defined less as a mortal-style personage than as a divine power: a will, office and creative theme made visible.
The sphere associated with Vairë is **Weaving, history and the tapestry of time**. Tolkien repeatedly presents the Valar through consorts, crafts, music, duties and the shape of their houses.

## Relationship to Middle-earth

The Valar are the Powers of the World who entered Arda after the Music of the Ainur. They oppose Melkor, preserve creation and generally act through delegated powers rather than constant direct rule.

## Selected Quotes

> Vairë the Weaver weaves all that has ever been in the halls of Mandos.

*The Silmarillion, Valaquenta.*

> The Valar, the Guardians of the World, are called the Powers of the World; they are the greatest of the Ainur who came to Arda.

*The Silmarillion, Valaquenta (condensed).*

> The Music of the Ainur brought Eä into being, and into its vision the Valar entered.

*The Silmarillion, Ainulindalë (condensed).*
